questions.q: In which year was The X-Men #1, Magneto's debut, cover-dated?
questions.why: Magneto appeared in the very first issue of The X-Men, cover-dated September 1963, as the team's first foe.

questions.q: Magneto's mutant power is the control of which natural force?
questions.why: Magneto can create and manipulate magnetic fields, which also lets him fly and move metal objects.

questions.q: What does Magneto's helmet protect him from?
questions.why: The helmet shields his mind from telepaths such as Professor X, which is why he rarely takes it off.

questions.q: In the comics, which Nazi concentration camp did young Max survive?
questions.why: Eisenhardt was imprisoned at Auschwitz as a boy of German Jewish descent, an experience that shapes his mutant-first outlook.

questions.q: Which actor played Magneto in the original 2000 X-Men movie?
questions.why: Ian McKellen played the older Magneto in Fox's X-Men films, while Michael Fassbender played the younger version.

questions.q: Which team of villains did Magneto found?
questions.why: Magneto formed the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants early on, with Quicksilver and Scarlet Witch among its first recruits.

questions.q: In the comics, which island nation did Magneto rule for a time?
questions.why: Magneto governed Genosha, a mutant haven that later suffered a devastating Sentinel attack.

questions.q: Which green-haired magnetic mutant is Magneto's daughter?
questions.why: Lorna Dane, who fights as Polaris, shares her father's command of magnetism.

questions.q: What was the name of Magneto's early orbital hideout, a hollowed-out rock?
questions.why: Asteroid M was a hollowed-out asteroid that served as Magneto's base in early stories.

questions.q: Who wrote the 2008 graphic novel Magneto: Testament, about Magneto's childhood?
questions.why: Greg Pak wrote Testament, a story of the young Max Eisenhardt built from Holocaust survivor accounts.

questions.q: In the comics, what is Magneto's birth name?
questions.why: He was born Max Eisenhardt; Erik Lehnsherr is a name he later adopted, the one the films use.
